title: Pop Culture Digest — Tuesday, October 20, 2026
description:
Tuesday · October 20, 2026
Pop Culture Digest
What’s actually dominating today
Tuesday’s conversation: Netflix finishes its executive purge by pushing out film chief Dan Lin, Miley Cyrus fires back at critics of her Hollywood Bowl comeback, Harry Styles debuts a song for Liam Payne at Madison Square Garden, U2 lands Netflix’s Thanksgiving Eve halftime show, and Hollywood says goodbye to Office Space’s Richard Riehle.
Streaming

Netflix pushes out film chief Dan Lin, completing a top-to-bottom content shakeup

Dan Lin is out as head of Netflix Film after about two and a half years, days after the streamer ousted chief content officer Bela Bajaria and laid off roughly 1,000 people, its biggest cut since 2022. Lin’s deputy Doug Belgrad and a run of senior TV executives are also gone. Peter Rice, the former Disney and Fox chief who takes over as chief content officer on Oct. 26, is expected to pick Lin’s replacement.

Lin was hired in 2024 to spend less on fewer, better movies. He reorganized the division by genre and leaned into mid-budget book adaptations and action films, while holding a hard line against theatrical-first releases. With subscriber and viewing growth stalled, Ted Sarandos told staff the new focus is “creating big, buzzy hits.” Lin thanked Sarandos, Greg Peters and Bajaria “for the opportunity.”

The Hollywood Reporter →   ·   Netflix’s Peter Rice announcement →   ·   The Wall Street Journal →

Music

Miley Cyrus fires back at critics of her Hollywood Bowl comeback and admits she almost didn’t go on

Friday’s Hollywood Bowl show was Cyrus’s first full live concert in four years, and clips of her skipping lines in hits like “Party in the USA” and “Flowers” drew pile-on commentary all weekend. At Sunday’s second show she addressed it head-on, joking mid-“Bass Persuades,” “Oh, I forgot I’m supposed to sing every fucking line!”

Then she got serious: “I’ve never heard that I don’t put my heart into something.” She said performing “does not come as natural as it once did,” and that before “Orbit” she had told herself she would run away instead of going on stage. “I can take a lot, but one thing I will not stand is any question about where my heart is when I’m on the stage. I am fully present.”

Listen on Spotify →   ·   Variety →

Music

Harry Styles premieres “Wise Enough,” a song for Liam Payne, at Madison Square Garden

Friday’s stop on Styles’s 30-night Together, Together residency fell on the second anniversary of Liam Payne’s death. Instead of his usual speech before “Sign of the Times,” Styles talked about losing a friend two years ago, then said, “I’m gonna sing a song I wrote two years ago for my friend,” and played a new ballad the room received in near silence and tears.

Fan videos spread all weekend, along with a debate over whether the title is “Wise Enough” or “What Is Enough?” He never said Payne’s name, which some fans criticized. The song hasn’t been released, so the Spotify link is his current album, Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally.

Listen on Spotify →   ·   Rolling Stone →

Streaming

U2 will headline Netflix’s first NFL Thanksgiving Eve halftime show

Netflix announced this morning that U2 will play halftime of the NFL’s first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game, Packers vs. Rams at SoFi Stadium on Nov. 25, as part of the band’s 50th anniversary. Kickoff is 8 p.m. ET (7 p.m. CT), and the game is included in every Netflix plan.

It’s U2’s first NFL halftime since Super Bowl XXXVI in 2002, the post-9/11 show where the names of victims scrolled behind the band. It continues Netflix’s run of big-name holiday halftimes after the Beyoncé Bowl in 2024 and Snoop Dogg’s Christmas show last year.

Listen on Spotify →   ·   Netflix Tudum →   ·   NFL.com →

Celebrities

Richard Riehle, Tom Smykowski in Office Space, dies at 78

Riehle, the character actor best known as the laid-off product manager with “people skills” in Mike Judge’s Office Space, died of natural causes Thursday in Los Angeles, his representatives confirmed Monday. He racked up more than 400 credits over nearly 50 years, including the guard who lets Harrison Ford escape in The Fugitive, the mechanic in Bridesmaids, Glory, and three Star Trek series.

He also played Donal Logue’s dad for five seasons of Grounded for Life. Logue called him “an actor’s actor — humble, kind, and incredible at his craft,” remembering the classic novel Riehle always kept in his back pocket.

Office Space trailer on YouTube →   ·   Los Angeles Times →

Bottom of the news

  • Taylor Swift’s “Patient Zero” holds No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 for a third week, while The Life of a Showgirl stays atop the Billboard 200.
  • Unconfirmed reports say Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are taking time apart after he liked a clip of Shane Gillis’s SNL monologue; neither has commented.
  • Selena Gomez says heavy nicotine vaping changed her voice and that she has quit.
  • Olivia Rodrigo’s art team posted behind-the-scenes footage to shoot down claims that the “expectations” video with Chappell Roan used AI.
  • Gwyneth Paltrow will star in A24’s drama series The Apology, her first lead TV role.
  • Rita Wilson says she’s returning for HBO’s five-episode Girls revival.
  • Jon Stewart will keep hosting The Daily Show on Mondays through 2028.
  • Rosie O’Donnell and Kristin Chenoweth join The Pyramid: An Unauthorized ‘Dance Moms’ Musical.
  • Mindy Kaling joins the cast of Running Point Season 3 as a gambling-app CEO.
